8	import {useEffect, useState} from 'react'
9	import {useVariant} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-variant'
10	import {useIntl} from 'react-intl'
11	import {useVariationParams} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-variation-params'
12	import {useVariationAttributes} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-variation-attributes'
13	import {useSelectedStore} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-selected-store'
14	
15	const OUT_OF_STOCK = 'OUT_OF_STOCK'
16	const UNFULFILLABLE = 'UNFULFILLABLE'
17	
18	const getInventoryById = (product, inventoryId) => {
19	    if (!inventoryId || !product?.inventories) {
20	        return null
21	    }
22	    return product.inventories.find((inv) => inv.id === inventoryId)
23	}
24	
25	// TODO: This needs to be refactored.
26	// If compatibility with API version < v8.1 is needed, keep pickupInStore as false
27	export const useDerivedProduct = (
28	    product,
29	    isProductPartOfSet = false,
30	    isProductPartOfBundle = false,
31	    pickupInStore = false,
32	    controlledVariationValues = null,
33	    onVariationChange = null
34	) => {
35	    const showLoading = !product
36	    const isProductABundle = product?.type?.bundle
37	    const stockLevel = product?.inventory?.stockLevel || 0
38	    const stepQuantity = product?.stepQuantity || 1
39	    const minOrderQuantity = stockLevel > 0 ? product?.minOrderQuantity || 1 : 0
40	    const initialQuantity = product?.quantity || product?.minOrderQuantity || 1
41	
42	    // used for product bundles when there are multiple products
43	    const lowestStockLevelProductName = product?.inventory?.lowestStockLevelProductName
44	    const intl = useIntl()
45	    const variant = useVariant(
46	        product,
47	        isProductPartOfSet,
48	        isProductPartOfBundle,
49	        controlledVariationValues
50	    )
51	    const isStandardProduct = product?.type?.item
52	    const variationParams = useVariationParams(
53	        product,
54	        isProductPartOfSet,
55	        isProductPartOfBundle,
56	        controlledVariationValues
57	    )
58	    const variationAttributes = useVariationAttributes(
59	        product,
60	        isProductPartOfSet,
61	        isProductPartOfBundle,
62	        controlledVariationValues,
63	        onVariationChange
64	    )
65	    const [quantity, setQuantity] = useState(initialQuantity)
66	    const {selectedStore} = useSelectedStore()
67	
68	    // A product is considered out of stock if the stock level is 0 or if we have all our
69	    // variation attributes selected, but don't have a variant. We do this because the API
70	    // will sometimes return all the variants even if they are out of stock, but for other
71	    // products it won't.
72	    const isOutOfStock =
73	        !stockLevel ||
74	        (!isProductABundle &&
75	            !variant &&
76	            !isStandardProduct &&
77	            Object.keys(variationParams).length === variationAttributes.length) ||
78	        (!isProductABundle && variant && !variant.orderable)
79	    const unfulfillable = stockLevel < quantity
80	
81	    // Product details for selected store
82	    const selectedStoreInventory = getInventoryById(product, selectedStore?.inventoryId)
83	    const selectedStoreStockLevel = selectedStoreInventory?.stockLevel || 0
84	    const selectedStoreLowestStockLevelProductName =
85	        selectedStoreInventory?.lowestStockLevelProductName
86	    // selectedStoreStockLevel and selectedStoreInventory are already variant specific,
87	    // so we don't need to check for variation attributes
88	    const isSelectedStoreOutOfStock = !selectedStoreStockLevel || !selectedStoreInventory?.orderable
89	    const selectedStoreUnfulfillable = selectedStoreStockLevel < quantity
90	
91	    // Use appropriate inventory based on pickup/delivery selection
92	    const currentStockLevel = pickupInStore ? selectedStoreStockLevel : stockLevel
93	    const currentLowestStockLevelProductName = pickupInStore
94	        ? selectedStoreLowestStockLevelProductName
95	        : lowestStockLevelProductName
96	    const currentIsOutOfStock = pickupInStore ? isSelectedStoreOutOfStock : isOutOfStock
97	    const currentUnfulfillable = pickupInStore ? selectedStoreUnfulfillable : unfulfillable
98	
99	    const inventoryMessages = {
100	        [OUT_OF_STOCK]: intl.formatMessage({
101	            defaultMessage: 'Out of stock',
102	            id: 'use_product.message.out_of_stock'
103	        }),
104	        [UNFULFILLABLE]: currentLowestStockLevelProductName
105	            ? intl.formatMessage(
106	                  {
107	                      defaultMessage: 'Only {stockLevel} left for {productName}!',
108	                      id: 'use_product.message.inventory_remaining_for_product'
109	                  },
110	                  {stockLevel: currentStockLevel, productName: currentLowestStockLevelProductName}
111	              )
112	            : intl.formatMessage(
113	                  {
114	                      defaultMessage: 'Only {stockLevel} left!',
115	                      id: 'use_product.message.inventory_remaining'
116	                  },
117	                  {stockLevel: currentStockLevel}
118	              )
119	    }
120	
121	    // showInventoryMessage controls if add to cart button is disabled
122	    const showInventoryMessage =
123	        (variant || isProductABundle || isStandardProduct) &&
124	        (currentIsOutOfStock || currentUnfulfillable)
125	    const inventoryMessage =
126	        (currentIsOutOfStock && inventoryMessages[OUT_OF_STOCK]) ||
127	        (currentUnfulfillable && inventoryMessages[UNFULFILLABLE])
128	
129	    // If the `initialQuantity` changes, update the state. This typically happens
130	    // when either the master product changes, or the inventory of the product changes
131	    // from out-of-stock to in-stock or vice versa.
132	    useEffect(() => {
133	        setQuantity(initialQuantity)
134	    }, [initialQuantity])
135	
136	    // Lump the out of stock/unfulfillable checks together for easier consumption
137	    return {
138	        showLoading,
139	        showInventoryMessage,
140	        inventoryMessage,
141	        variationAttributes,
142	        quantity,
143	        minOrderQuantity,
144	        stepQuantity,
145	        variationParams,
146	        setQuantity,
147	        variant,
148	        stockLevel,
149	        isOutOfStock,
150	        unfulfillable,
151	        isSelectedStoreOutOfStock: isSelectedStoreOutOfStock || selectedStoreUnfulfillable,
152	        selectedStore
153	    }
154	}

8	/*
9	 * Copy-first port of node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-image.jsx
10	 * (retail-react-app 10.0.0), converted to TypeScript per AGENTS.md's copy-first rule (SFCC-270,
11	 * plan step 2.1). Zero functional diff at that step beyond the TypeScript annotations and a
12	 * temporary `[overrides]` console.log marker (verified live, then removed).
13	 *
14	 * `useItemVariant` is already imported via the relative `'.'` in the base file — unchanged here.
15	 *
16	 * SFCC-270 (plan step 2.2): restyled to the Figma cart-item spec. The outer Box's own literal
17	 * `width="84px" backgroundColor="gray.100"` defaults are gone, replaced by item-variant.css.ts's
18	 * `image` part via `__css` — kept as `__css`, not `sx`, specifically so a caller-supplied
19	 * `width`/`mr` (e.g. order-summary/index.jsx's base, not-yet-overridden
20	 * `<CartItemVariantImage width="80px" mr={2} />`) still wins; see that recipe's own docblock for
21	 * why. `{...props}` stays spread last, same defaults-then-spread order as before, still what
22	 * lets that caller-supplied width win. `ratio`'s default changed from `1` to the Figma-confirmed
23	 * 288/432 cart-item image ratio; the inner <Image> now also carries the `img` part's responsive
24	 * objectFit + mix-blend-multiply. Badge styling (Sale/Unavailable) is untouched — no Figma value
25	 * was given for it at this step.
26	 */
27	import React from 'react';
28	import {
29	  AspectRatio,
30	  Box,
31	  Badge,
32	  Image,
33	  useMultiStyleConfig,
34	} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';
35	import { useItemVariant } from '.';
36	import { FormattedMessage } from 'react-intl';
37	import { findImageGroupBy } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/image-groups-utils';
38	// Recipe key — single source in item-variant.css.ts (SFCC-270 round 2 rework), no longer
39	// redeclared per file.
40	import { ZIMM_CART_ITEM_VARIANT_RECIPE } from './item-variant.css';
41	
42	// See index.tsx's own note on why this is `any` rather than a structural type.
43	type SfccVariant = any;
44	
45	type ItemImageProps = {
46	  imageProps?: Record<string, any>;
47	  ratio?: number;
48	} & Record<string, any>;
49	
50	// Figma "Image" spec, product-item card (SFCC-270): aspect ratio 288/432, which reduces to 2/3
51	// exactly. Matches the design record's own 132x198 desktop pair exactly (132 * 432/288 = 198);
52	// against the 67x100 mobile pair it lands at 100.5 — half a pixel over the stated 100, the same
53	// class of Figma-rounding gap zimmDrawer.css.ts's WIDTH_XLARGE note already documents for a
54	// different value, not something introduced here.
55	const CART_ITEM_IMAGE_RATIO = 288 / 432;
56	
57	/**
58	 * In the context of a cart product item variant, this component renders the item's
59	 * main image.
60	 *
61	 * @todo = This component will render a `SALE` badge when the qualifier is available
62	 * on the custom property `c_isSale`. This will need to be expanded upon to handle
63	 * different badge/qualifiers and property names.
64	 */
65	const ItemImage = ({ imageProps, ratio = CART_ITEM_IMAGE_RATIO, ...props }: ItemImageProps) => {
66	  const variant: SfccVariant = useItemVariant();
67	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_ITEM_VARIANT_RECIPE, {});
68	
69	  // We find the 'small' images in the variant's image groups based on variationValues and pick the first one
70	  const image = findImageGroupBy(variant?.imageGroups, {
71	    viewType: 'small',
72	    selectedVariationAttributes: variant?.variationValues,
73	  })?.images?.[0];
74	
75	  return (
76	    <Box __css={styles.image} {...props}>
77	      <AspectRatio ratio={ratio}>
78	        <Box position="relative">
79	          {variant.c_isSale && (
80	            <Badge
81	              position="absolute"
82	              top={0}
83	              left={0}
84	              marginLeft={2}
85	              marginTop={2}
86	              fontSize="10px"
87	              variant="solid"
88	              colorScheme="blue"
89	            >
90	              <FormattedMessage
91	                defaultMessage="Sale"
92	                id="item_image.label.sale"
93	                description="A sale badge placed on top of a product image"
94	              />
95	            </Badge>
96	          )}
97	          {variant.isProductUnavailable && (
98	            <Badge
99	              position="absolute"
100	              top={0}
101	              left={0}
102	              marginLeft={2}
103	              marginTop={2}
104	              fontSize="10px"
105	              variant="solid"
106	              colorScheme="red"
107	            >
108	              <FormattedMessage
109	                defaultMessage="Unavailable"
110	                id="item_image.label.unavailable"
111	                description="A unavailable badge placed on top of a product image"
112	              />
113	            </Badge>
114	          )}
115	
116	          {image && (
117	            <Image
118	              alt={image.alt}
119	              src={`${image.disBaseLink || image.link}`}
120	              ignoreFallback={true}
121	              __css={styles.img}
122	              {...imageProps}
123	            />
124	          )}
125	        </Box>
126	      </AspectRatio>
127	    </Box>
128	  );
129	};
130	
131	export default ItemImage;
132

8	/*
9	 * Copy-first port of node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-name.jsx
10	 * (retail-react-app 10.0.0), converted to TypeScript per AGENTS.md's copy-first rule (SFCC-270,
11	 * plan step 2.1). Zero functional diff at that step beyond the TypeScript annotation and a
12	 * temporary `[overrides]` console.log marker (verified live, then removed).
13	 *
14	 * `useItemVariant` is already imported via the relative `'.'` in the base file — unchanged here.
15	 * `Link` is not overridden anywhere in this repo (verified by directory listing at time of
16	 * writing), so it stays on the base `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` path.
17	 *
18	 * SFCC-270 (plan step 2.2), bug fix: base had `<Link {...props} color="black.600" to={...}>` —
19	 * spreading `props` BEFORE the explicit `color`/`to`, the opposite order from item-image/
20	 * item-attributes/item-price's own `{...props}` placement (spread last), so a caller-supplied
21	 * `color` was silently overridden here instead of taking precedence, unlike those three
22	 * siblings. Fixed by moving `color` ahead of the spread, matching the siblings' order — `to`
23	 * stays after the spread, unchanged, since it is data-derived (from `productId`) and was never
24	 * meant to be caller-overridable the way `color` is. No current base caller passes `color`, so
25	 * nothing observable changes for them; this only matters going forward.
26	 *
27	 * Also restyled per the Figma cart-item spec: `fontSize="md"` (a bare Chakra token — this
28	 * repo's own `fontSizes` scale is deliberately NOT registered as `theme.fontSizes`, see
29	 * typography.ts, so that literal was silently reading Chakra's own unrelated default) replaced
30	 * by `textStyle="productNames"`, which also carries the spec's "uppercase" requirement (see
31	 * typography.ts's `productNames` entry). The bug-fixed default colour is expressed as a literal
32	 * `var(--zimm-color-text-default)` prop rather than routed through the recipe: a plain literal
33	 * prop is provably override-safe here regardless of `Link`'s own internal implementation (it
34	 * lands in the same `props` bucket a caller's own `color` would use), where `__css`/`sx` on this
35	 * specific base `Link` wrapper is not — see item-variant.css.ts's own docblock for the
36	 * `__css`-discarding hazard that rules `__css` out for a plain Chakra `Text`, a nearby but
37	 * distinct case worth being equally careful about here.
38	 *
39	 * Figma-fidelity audit fix, 2026-09-19: the element rendering `textStyle="productNames"` was
40	 * Chakra's own `Heading` (imported from `shared/ui`), not a plain element. `Heading` carries its
41	 * own registered theme (`baseStyle: {fontWeight: 'bold'}` plus a `size`-keyed `fontSize`/
42	 * `lineHeight` map, resolved internally via `useStyleConfig`) — with no `size` prop supplied, that
43	 * defaulted to Chakra's own `lg`-equivalent (`fontSize: 3xl`/30px, `lineHeight: 1.33`/39.9px,
44	 * `fontWeight: bold`/700), which the external `textStyle` prop sits alongside rather than
45	 * overrides. Measured live (Storybook, real Chromium): rendered 30px/700/39.9px against a
46	 * 14px/500/16px spec — confirmed via a real screenshot, not inferred. `chakra.h2` carries no such
47	 * internal styling, so `textStyle` is the only style source and cannot be out-ranked — the same
48	 * reasoning `ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductName`'s own docblock already states for why it uses a plain
49	 * `chakra.p`, not `Heading`, for this exact reason. `as="h2"` is preserved so the semantic/
50	 * accessible heading level is unchanged; only the underlying styled-component source of the
51	 * conflict is removed.
52	 */
53	import React from 'react';
54	import { useItemVariant } from '.';
55	import Link from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/link';
56	import { chakra } from '@chakra-ui/react';
57	
58	/**
59	 * In the context of a cart product item variant, this components simply renders
60	 * the item's name using the cart item field `productName`. We use this field
61	 * rather than variant `name` field as the variant detail may not yet be
62	 * available upon rendering.
63	 */
64	const ItemName = (props: Record<string, any>) => {
65	  const variant = useItemVariant();
66	  const productId = variant?.master?.masterId || variant.id;
67	
68	  return (
69	    <chakra.h2 textStyle="productNames">
70	      <Link color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" {...props} to={`/product/${productId}`}>
71	        {variant.productName || variant.name}
72	      </Link>
73	    </chakra.h2>
74	  );
75	};
76	
77	export default ItemName;
78

 * siblings. Fixed by moving `color` ahead of the spread, matching the siblings' order — `to`
 * stays after the spread, unchanged, since it is data-derived (from `productId`) and was never
 * meant to be caller-overridable the way `color` is. No current base caller passes `color`, so
 * nothing observable changes for them; this only matters going forward.
 *
 * Also restyled per the Figma cart-item spec: `fontSize="md"` (a bare Chakra token — this
 * repo's own `fontSizes` scale is deliberately NOT registered as `theme.fontSizes`, see
 * typography.ts, so that literal was silently reading Chakra's own unrelated default) replaced
 * by `textStyle="productNames"`, which also carries the spec's "uppercase" requirement (see
 * typography.ts's `productNames` entry). The bug-fixed default colour is expressed as a literal
 * `var(--zimm-color-text-default)` prop rather than routed through the recipe: a plain literal
 * prop is provably override-safe here regardless of `Link`'s own internal implementation (it
 * lands in the same `props` bucket a caller's own `color` would use), where `__css`/`sx` on this
 * specific base `Link` wrapper is not — see item-variant.css.ts's own docblock for the
 * `__css`-discarding hazard that rules `__css` out for a plain Chakra `Text`, a nearby but
 * distinct case worth being equally careful about here.
 *
 * Figma-fidelity audit fix, 2026-09-19: the element rendering `textStyle="productNames"` was
 * Chakra's own `Heading` (imported from `shared/ui`), not a plain element. `Heading` carries its
 * own registered theme (`baseStyle: {fontWeight: 'bold'}` plus a `size`-keyed `fontSize`/
 * `lineHeight` map, resolved internally via `useStyleConfig`) — with no `size` prop supplied, that
 * defaulted to Chakra's own `lg`-equivalent (`fontSize: 3xl`/30px, `lineHeight: 1.33`/39.9px,
 * `fontWeight: bold`/700), which the external `textStyle` prop sits alongside rather than
 * overrides. Measured live (Storybook, real Chromium): rendered 30px/700/39.9px against a
 * 14px/500/16px spec — confirmed via a real screenshot, not inferred. `chakra.h2` carries no such
 * internal styling, so `textStyle` is the only style source and cannot be out-ranked — the same
 * reasoning `ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductName`'s own docblock already states for why it uses a plain
 * `chakra.p`, not `Heading`, for this exact reason. `as="h2"` is preserved so the semantic/
 * accessible heading level is unchanged; only the underlying styled-component source of the
 * conflict is removed.

import React from 'react';
import { useItemVariant } from '.';
import Link from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/link';
import { chakra } from '@chakra-ui/react';

/**
 * In the context of a cart product item variant, this components simply renders
 * the item's name using the cart item field `productName`. We use this field
 * rather than variant `name` field as the variant detail may not yet be
 * available upon rendering.
 */
const ItemName = (props: Record<string, any>) => {
  const variant = useItemVariant();
  const productId = variant?.master?.masterId || variant.id;

  return (
    <chakra.h2 textStyle="productNames">
      <Link color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" {...props} to={`/product/${productId}`}>
        {variant.productName || variant.name}
      </Link>
    </chakra.h2>
  );
};

export default ItemName;

2	import { QueryClient, QueryClientProvider } from '@tanstack/react-query';
3	import { renderHook, type RenderHookOptions } from '@testing-library/react';
4	
5	/**
6	 * Builds a fresh QueryClient per call — test isolation, no cache bleed between tests.
7	 * Matches `_app-config/index.tsx`'s real `defaultOptions` for retry/refetchOnWindowFocus so a
8	 * hook under test behaves the same as it does in the running app.
9	 */
10	const createTestQueryClient = () =>
11	  new QueryClient({
12	    defaultOptions: {
13	      queries: { retry: false, refetchOnWindowFocus: false },
14	    },
15	  });
16	
17	/**
18	 * Renders a hook that calls `@tanstack/react-query`'s `useQuery` inside a fresh
19	 * `QueryClientProvider` — the same wrapper `_app-config`'s `withReactQuery(AppConfig, ...)`
20	 * mounts for every page in the real app, so a hook under test needs no provider of its own
21	 * beyond this. See `.claude/rules/testing.md` > Commerce SDK hooks for the equivalent
22	 * `renderWithProviders` pattern this mirrors for `CommerceApiProvider`-dependent hooks.
23	 *
24	 * @param callback the hook to render
25	 * @param options `renderHook` options other than `wrapper`, which this helper supplies
26	 * @returns the same result `@testing-library/react`'s `renderHook` returns
27	 */
28	export const renderHookWithQueryClient = <TResult, TProps>(
29	  callback: (props: TProps) => TResult,
30	  options?: Omit<RenderHookOptions<TProps>, 'wrapper'>,
31	) => {
32	  const queryClient = createTestQueryClient();
33	  return renderHook(callback, {
34	    ...options,
35	    wrapper: ({ children }) => <QueryClientProvider client={queryClient}>{children}</QueryClientProvider>,
36	  });
37	};

1	import React from 'react';
2	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
3	import { ZimmDrawer } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer';
4	
5	const ZIMM_CART_DRAWER_RECIPE = 'ZimmCartDrawer';
6	
7	export type ZimmCartDrawerProps = {
8	  /** Whether the drawer is open. */
9	  isOpen: boolean;
10	  /** Called on backdrop click, Escape, and the close button (all via ZimmDrawer/Chakra's Drawer). */
11	  onClose: () => void;
12	  /** Number of line items in the bag. Drives the header title only ("BAG • {itemCount}" vs
13	   *  "YOUR BAG IS EMPTY") — see `children`'s own doc below for the empty-vs-populated body. */
14	  itemCount: number;
15	  /** Element to focus once the drawer finishes closing — see ZimmDrawer's own doc (AC10
16	   *  focus-return); without this Chakra falls back to focusing document.body. */
17	  finalFocusRef?: React.RefObject<HTMLElement>;
18	  /** Cart line items — or the empty-state body. This organism owns no item-rendering logic and
19	   *  no empty-vs-populated decision itself: it renders whatever `children` it is given,
20	   *  unconditionally, regardless of `itemCount`. The caller (`cartDrawerContainer.tsx`, SFCC-11
21	   *  plan step 4.6) decides between the real item list and `ZimmCartEmptyState`. */
22	  children: React.ReactNode;
23	  /** Reserved slot for SFCC-404's message-aggregation system (validation/error/promo banners).
24	   *  Always rendered, even with nothing passed — see zimmCartDrawer.css.ts's `messages` part:
25	   *  the band reserves height regardless, so the drawer doesn't change position when a message
26	   *  appears or disappears. */
27	  messages?: React.ReactNode;
28	  /** Reserved slot for SFCC-275's button group (checkout / continue shopping). Not built in this
29	   *  commit (SFCC-315 is shell-only) — this organism only provides the slot it will render into
30	   *  later. */
31	  footer?: React.ReactNode;
32	};
33	
34	/**
35	 * SFCC-315 — the Cart drawer shell. Wraps ZimmDrawer (size="xLarge") with the cart-specific
36	 * header title, a height-reserving messages band, a responsive items/totals layout, and a
37	 * footer slot.
38	 *
39	 * Deliberately not wired to a trigger yet — no `_app`/`product-view` changes, no
40	 * `useCartDrawer` hook, no button-group content, no real empty-state body, no message
41	 * aggregation. All of those are separate, later commits in this same 18-commit plan — this
42	 * organism is exercised only via its own Storybook stories today.
43	 *
44	 * Figma-fidelity audit fix, 2026-09-19: `ZimmDrawer`'s `title` was passed with no `titleStyle`,
45	 * so it silently took that prop's default (`'large'` → `heading1`, 24px) instead of the Figma
46	 * spec for this header ("BAG • #", 14px medium — `body2Strong`). Measured live before the fix:
47	 * 24px/400/32px against the 14px/500 spec. `ZimmDrawer` itself already supports both correctly
48	 * (`titleStyle="small"` → `body2Strong`, confirmed against `typography.ts`) — this was a missing
49	 * prop at the call site, not a defect in `ZimmDrawer`.
50	 *
51	 * @param props see ZimmCartDrawerProps
52	 */
53	export const ZimmCartDrawer = ({
54	  isOpen,
55	  onClose,
56	  itemCount,
57	  finalFocusRef,
58	  children,
59	  messages,
60	  footer,
61	}: ZimmCartDrawerProps) => {
62	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_DRAWER_RECIPE, {});
63	  const title = itemCount === 0 ? 'YOUR BAG IS EMPTY' : `BAG • ${itemCount}`;
64	
65	  return (
66	    <ZimmDrawer
67	      isOpen={isOpen}
68	      onClose={onClose}
69	      size="xLarge"
70	      title={title}
71	      titleStyle="small"
72	      finalFocusRef={finalFocusRef}
73	    >
74	      <chakra.div __css={styles.messages}>{messages}</chakra.div>
75	      <chakra.div __css={styles.body}>
76	        {itemCount === 0 ? <chakra.p textStyle="body2">{EMPTY_BAG_PLACEHOLDER_TEXT}</chakra.p> : children}
77	      </chakra.div>
78	      <chakra.div __css={styles.footer}>{footer}</chakra.div>
79	    </ZimmDrawer>
80	  );
81	};

input.message:
Step 4.6 implemented on `feature/SFCC-11_cart` (confirmed not on develop/main before starting). Nothing staged or committed — working tree only.

## Files touched

**Created:**
- `overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx` (431 lines) — the container.
- `overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.test.tsx` (588 lines, 20 tests).

**Modified (Required fix #1, disclosed plainly, not buried):**
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/index.tsx` — removed the `itemCount === 0 ? <hardcoded placeholder> : children` ternary and the dead `EMPTY_BAG_PLACEHOLDER_TEXT` constant; body now renders `{children}` unconditionally. Updated three doc comments that were describing the old, now-wrong behaviour (the `children`/`itemCount` prop docs and the top-of-file "not wired to a trigger yet" paragraph, which used to list "no real empty-state body" as still-missing).
- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/index.test.tsx` — added two new tests proving `children` renders regardless of `itemCount` (including at 0). **Correction to the brief/plan text**: I read this file in full before touching it — there was no pre-existing assertion on the old hardcoded placeholder text to "update" (only header-title tests existed, which check a different prop entirely, the dialog's accessible name). The plan's claim that one existed doesn't hold against the real file; I added the missing assertion rather than stopping, since the pass criterion itself (assert children renders unconditionally) is unambiguous and this doesn't touch anything outside the manifest. Flagging it here rather than silently absorbing it.

## The wishlist-drawer question (fourth open question)

Resolved as: this container calls `useWishlistAuthDrawer()` directly (not the `<ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer>` wrapper) and renders the wrapper's own UI composition itself (`ZimmDrawer` → `ErrorFallback` → `ZimmAuthDrawerContent`, plus `AuthModal`/`OtpAuth`) in a small internal sub-component (`CartWishlistAuthGate`, same file). This is a disclosed, deliberate duplication of `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer`'s render body — that file is outside this step's manifest and its `children: React.ReactElement` contract is structurally single-trigger, so there's no lower-risk shared extraction point available from here.

**Focus-return story (AC10), stated plainly**: every row's `onGuestWishlistClick` calls `handleTriggerClick({currentTarget: document.body})` — a fabricated minimal event, not a real one. I deliberately did **not** use `document.activeElement` as a "probably fine" substitute, even though it would often hold the real clicked row's link: `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own `handleTriggerClick` comment already explains why it chose `e.currentTarget` over `document.activeElement` for this identical job — "unlike document.activeElement which may still be body on click." Building on a mechanism that file's own author already rejected would trade an honest degradation for a silently unreliable one. `document.body` instead matches an **already-established** fallback in this exact codebase — `ZimmCartDrawer`'s own prop doc: "without this Chakra falls back to focusing document.body." So: closing the auth drawer after a guest wishlist click returns focus to the page body, not back to the specific row that was clicked. Single-trigger callers (header/PDP wishlist icon) are unaffected — they still go through the unmodified `<ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer>`.

## Pass criterion 4 — how far it's proven

Mechanism: `hasPendingPostAuthSettleRef` (a **ref**, not state) is set by `onAuthSuccess`; a gating `useEffect` (deps `[isRegistered, useIsMutating(), queryClient]`) only flips `isGuestState` to `false` once `isRegistered` is true **and** (`!hasPendingPostAuthSettleRef.current` **or** a live `queryClient.isMutating() === 0`). The ref (not `useState`) matters because `useWishlistAuthDrawer()` is called *before* this effect in the same component, so within one commit its internal effect (which calls `onAuthSuccess` then `mergeBasket.mutate()`) runs first — a `setState` there wouldn't be visible to this effect until a *later* render, but a ref write is visible immediately, in the same flush.

Proven: a controlled-timing test holds a live `queryClient.isMutating` spy at 1, confirms `isGuest` stays `true` after the captured `onAuthSuccess` fires, then drops the spy to 0 and confirms it flips to `false`. Mutation-tested — deleting the wait condition entirely fails this test.

**Disclosed limitation, found by actually attempting the mutation, not assumed**: this test does *not* distinguish the ref from a plain `useState` for the same flag — swapping one for the other leaves the suite green, because the test invokes the captured `onAuthSuccess` as a plain synchronous call from test code (not as a second real internal effect racing this one in the same commit), so it can't reproduce the specific same-commit ordering the ref exists for. The ref's necessity is a reasoned argument about React's real effect-scheduling order (documented in both the code comment and the test's own comment), not something this Vitest suite mechanically proves. I did the reasoning through carefully and I'm confident in it, but I'm not overstating what the automated test covers.

## Pass criteria — status

1. **One `ProductItem` per line, mapped via `cartItemMapper` verbatim** — proven. `selectCartItemProps`' output supplies `productId`/`name` to `ZimmCartItemActions` (test computes the same values independently via the real, unmocked mapper and asserts equality). `ProductItem`'s own `product` prop is a separate merge (base `pages/cart/index.jsx`'s own precedent, minus `allImages`/bundle handling) — see correction below.
2. **Render guard runs from an effect, no-ops under `useIsMutating()`** — proven, and the "effect not render body" half was caught **failing to actually prove itself** on the first pass (see below) before I fixed it.
3. **`secondaryActions` is real, wired `ZimmCartItemActions`** — proven. Remove/wishlist-move click through mocked `ZimmCartItemActions` to real `removeItemFromBasketMutation.mutateAsync`/`createCustomerProductListItem.mutateAsync` calls with asserted exact args; already-in-wishlist short-circuit proven.
4. **Resumed wishlist-move waits for merge+cap** — proven per above, with the disclosed ref-vs-state limitation.
5. **Empty basket → `ZimmCartEmptyState`** — proven with the real (unmocked) `ZimmCartDrawer`, mutation-tested against the reverted placeholder.
6. **Footer → `ZimmCartButtonGroup`; messages omitted** — footer proven directly. Messages: I initially wrote a weak assertion (`not.toHaveTextContent(/undefined/)`) that doesn't actually prove anything, caught it on review, and replaced it — the honest fact is that "omitted" and "explicitly passed `messages={undefined}`" render byte-identical output, so no runtime test can distinguish them; the real proof is `grep -n "messages" cartDrawerContainer.tsx` returning zero matches, which I did and state directly in the test's own comment.
7. **Container owns no `isOpen`/`onClose` state** — proven (prop passthrough both ways).
8. **Exactly one production `<ZimmCartDrawer` call site** — verified directly: `grep -rn "<ZimmCartDrawer" overrides/app` returns the container plus `ZimmCartDrawer`'s own stories/tests only.

**A real correction against the plan's own text, found by reading base code in full rather than trusting the paraphrase**: Required fix #2 describes base's `productsByItemId[productItem.itemId]` lookup. Reading `node_modules/.../pages/cart/index.jsx` in full shows that map is a *second*, separate `useMemo` that exists only to support bundle-child-inventory enrichment (out of this step's scope) — the actual `useProducts` fetch underneath it is keyed by **productId**, not itemId. My container looks the fetched product up by `productId` directly; no intermediate re-keyed map. Also found: the plan's Changes text says "this container... calls `useCartMessages`'s three functions" — checking `zimmCartItemActions/index.tsx`'s real current code shows it already calls `notifyAddedToWishlist`/`notifyAlreadyInWishlist` itself (step 4.4). This container only fires `notifyMaxQuantityReached` (the one function with no other call site) — calling the other two here as well would double-fire the toast. Both corrections are cited with file:line in the code comments, not just asserted.

## Deliberately out of scope (disclosed, not silently dropped)

- **`onItemQuantityChange` is not wired to a real mutation.** No pass criterion, Changes item, or Tester check for this step names it, and no other plan step claims it either. `ProductItem`'s own no-op default applies, so the quantity stepper in the cart drawer only updates local state this commit — a shopper's quantity edit does not persist server-side yet. This is a real, material gap I chose not to take on unasked rather than silently expand scope.
- Per-line "isRemoving" spinner feedback (base's own pattern) — not reproduced, not asked for.

## Gate output

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean, whole repo.
- `npm run test` — **124 test files, 1726 tests, all passed**, including `zimmCartDrawer`'s full existing suite (12/12, re-run per verification standard #6 since I touched its focus/render logic) and `recipeGuards.test.ts` (6/6).
- `npx eslint` on all four touched files — clean (0 errors, 0 warnings) after fixing 6 prettier errors and 5 type-safety warnings the first pass surfaced.
- `npm run audit:tokens` — zero violations attributed to either of my two production files (`cartDrawerContainer.tsx`, `zimmCartDrawer/index.tsx`); the 9 unacknowledged pre-existing violations reported are all in files I never touched.
- `grep -rn "<ZimmCartDrawer" overrides/app` — exactly one production call site (this container), plus `ZimmCartDrawer`'s own stories/test.
- No `.stories.tsx` in this step's manifest — correctly so: this is a `pages/cart/` container, not a `ui-kits/` component, and components.md's story requirement is about exported components under `overrides/app/components/`/`overrides/app/pages/` more broadly ("Pages get a story showing the full assembly") — but this container isn't itself a page (base `pages/cart/index.jsx` still is), it's a piece one mounts *inside* `_app` (step 9, not yet built). I did not add one since nothing in the manifest or pass criteria calls for it and there's no page-level assembly point yet to story against; flagging this reasoning rather than silently skipping the question.
- Mutation-tested three things directly (revert, confirm red; restore, confirm green): the `ZimmCartDrawer` children-vs-placeholder fix, the render-guard's effect-vs-render-body wiring, and the pass-criterion-4 wait mechanism. The render-guard test failed to catch its own regression on the first attempt — I caught this by actually performing the mutation rather than trusting the assertion, and rewrote it to force a genuine second render and assert the call count stays at one.

## My own unverified gaps

- I did not verify real-browser AC10 focus-return behaviour for the `document.body` degradation (no live browser check, jsdom can't meaningfully exercise this either) — the reasoning is sound but untested live.
- I did not add Storybook coverage for `CartWishlistAuthGate` (the internal sub-component) — it's not exported, has no independent contract, and components.md's story rule doesn't reach internal sub-components used by only one parent.
- The theoretical micro-window in `useCartMergeAndCap.capBasketQuantities`'s own mutation-in-flight self-check (a brief instant between the merge mutation settling and the cap mutation starting where `isMutating()` could read 0) is pre-existing, already-shipped behaviour from step 4.2, not something this step touches or was asked to fix — noting it for completeness, not as my own gap.

## What Marcel is missing

Nothing this pass that isn't already named above or in the plan's own open questions — but worth restating plainly since it's easy to lose in the detail: the quantity stepper in the cart drawer will visibly work (buttons respond, number changes) while doing nothing to the real basket. That's a genuine, silent-looking gap for whoever tests this build casually, and no step currently on the board claims it.

5. **Empty basket → `ZimmCartEmptyState`** — proven with the real (unmocked) `ZimmCartDrawer`, mutation-tested against the reverted placeholder.
6. **Footer → `ZimmCartButtonGroup`; messages omitted** — footer proven directly. Messages: I initially wrote a weak assertion (`not.toHaveTextContent(/undefined/)`) that doesn't actually prove anything, caught it on review, and replaced it — the honest fact is that "omitted" and "explicitly passed `messages={undefined}`" render byte-identical output, so no runtime test can distinguish them; the real proof is `grep -n "messages" cartDrawerContainer.tsx` returning zero matches, which I did and state directly in the test's own comment.
7. **Container owns no `isOpen`/`onClose` state** — proven (prop passthrough both ways).
8. **Exactly one production `<ZimmCartDrawer` call site** — verified directly: `grep -rn "<ZimmCartDrawer" overrides/app` returns the container plus `ZimmCartDrawer`'s own stories/tests only.

**A real correction against the plan's own text, found by reading base code in full rather than trusting the paraphrase**: Required fix #2 describes base's `productsByItemId[productItem.itemId]` lookup. Reading `node_modules/.../pages/cart/index.jsx` in full shows that map is a *second*, separate `useMemo` that exists only to support bundle-child-inventory enrichment (out of this step's scope) — the actual `useProducts` fetch underneath it is keyed by **productId**, not itemId. My container looks the fetched product up by `productId` directly; no intermediate re-keyed map. Also found: the plan's Changes text says "this container... calls `useCartMessages`'s three functions" — checking `zimmCartItemActions/index.tsx`'s real current code shows it already calls `notifyAddedToWishlist`/`notifyAlreadyInWishlist` itself (step 4.4). This container only fires `notifyMaxQuantityReached` (the one function with no other call site) — calling the other two here as well would double-fire the toast. Both corrections are cited with file:line in the code comments, not just asserted.

## Deliberately out of scope (disclosed, not silently dropped)

- **`onItemQuantityChange` is not wired to a real mutation.** No pass criterion, Changes item, or Tester check for this step names it, and no other plan step claims it either. `ProductItem`'s own no-op default applies, so the quantity stepper in the cart drawer only updates local state this commit — a shopper's quantity edit does not persist server-side yet. This is a real, material gap I chose not to take on unasked rather than silently expand scope.
- Per-line "isRemoving" spinner feedback (base's own pattern) — not reproduced, not asked for.

## Gate output

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean, whole repo.
- `npm run test` — **124 test files, 1726 tests, all passed**, including `zimmCartDrawer`'s full existing suite (12/12, re-run per verification standard #6 since I touched its focus/render logic) and `recipeGuards.test.ts` (6/6).
- `npx eslint` on all four touched files — clean (0 errors, 0 warnings) after fixing 6 prettier errors and 5 type-safety warnings the first pass surfaced.
- `npm run audit:tokens` — zero violations attributed to either of my two production files (`cartDrawerContainer.tsx`, `zimmCartDrawer/index.tsx`); the 9 unacknowledged pre-existing violations reported are all in files I never touched.
- `grep -rn "<ZimmCartDrawer" overrides/app` — exactly one production call site (this container), plus `ZimmCartDrawer`'s own stories/test.
- No `.stories.tsx` in this step's manifest — correctly so: this is a `pages/cart/` container, not a `ui-kits/` component, and components.md's story requirement is about exported components under `overrides/app/components/`/`overrides/app/pages/` more broadly ("Pages get a story showing the full assembly") — but this container isn't itself a page (base `pages/cart/index.jsx` still is), it's a piece one mounts *inside* `_app` (step 9, not yet built). I did not add one since nothing in the manifest or pass criteria calls for it and there's no page-level assembly point yet to story against; flagging this reasoning rather than silently skipping the question.
- Mutation-tested three things directly (revert, confirm red; restore, confirm green): the `ZimmCartDrawer` children-vs-placeholder fix, the render-guard's effect-vs-render-body wiring, and the pass-criterion-4 wait mechanism. The render-guard test failed to catch its own regression on the first attempt — I caught this by actually performing the mutation rather than trusting the assertion, and rewrote it to force a genuine second render and assert the call count stays at one.

## My own unverified gaps

- I did not verify real-browser AC10 focus-return behaviour for the `document.body` degradation (no live browser check, jsdom can't meaningfully exercise this either) — the reasoning is sound but untested live.
- I did not add Storybook coverage for `CartWishlistAuthGate` (the internal sub-component) — it's not exported, has no independent contract, and components.md's story rule doesn't reach internal sub-components used by only one parent.
- The theoretical micro-window in `useCartMergeAndCap.capBasketQuantities`'s own mutation-in-flight self-check (a brief instant between the merge mutation settling and the cap mutation starting where `isMutating()` could read 0) is pre-existing, already-shipped behaviour from step 4.2, not something this step touches or was asked to fix — noting it for completeness, not as my own gap.

## What Marcel is missing

Nothing this pass that isn't already named above or in the plan's own open questions — but worth restating plainly since it's easy to lose in the detail: the quantity stepper in the cart drawer will visibly work (buttons respond, number changes) while doing nothing to the real basket. That's a genuine, silent-looking gap for whoever tests this build casually, and no step currently on the board claims it.
